cards.title: Introduction to Vue Performance
cards.content:
Performance is crucial for user retention and SEO. In Vue.js, optimization covers bundle size reduction, efficient reactivity usage, and runtime rendering speedups.

We will explore techniques like code splitting, lazy loading, and avoiding unnecessary re-renders.

cards.title: Using v-memo
cards.content:
Vue 3.2 introduced v-memo, which allows you to memoize a sub-tree of the template. It caches the DOM nodes based on a dependency array.

<div v-for="item in list" :key="item.id" v-memo="[item.id === selectedId]">
  <p>ID: {{ item.id }}</p>
</div>

cards.title: Caching Components with KeepAlive
cards.content:
When switching between dynamic components, you can keep inactive components alive in memory rather than destroying them by wrapping them in a <KeepAlive> tag.

<KeepAlive include="UserProfile,Settings">
  <component :is="currentView" />
</KeepAlive>

options.text: Computed properties are cached based on their reactive dependencies, whereas methods run every time they are called.
Methods are cached, but computed properties are not.
There is no performance difference between computed properties and methods.

cards.title: Summary of Best Practices
cards.content:
To keep your Vue applications lightning fast:

  • Leverage route-based code splitting.
  • Use shallowRef or shallowReactive for large immutable data structures.
  • Virtualize long lists.
  • Profile regularly using Vue Devtools and browser performance tabs.
